case.title: Tariq Khan v. Capital Development Authority
case.summary: Petitioner seeks a permanent injunction restraining the CDA from demolishing a commercial property in Sector F-7, Islamabad, alleging valid lease deed and procedural non-compliance.

verdict.judge_remarks: Counsel raised a valid constitutional touchstone under Article 4, but the presentation collapsed entirely during witness examination. Rather than eliciting the revenue entries favorable to the petitioner, counsel stubbornly insisted on cross-examining the witness on events at the physical site that the witness had repeatedly disclaimed witnessing. Consequently, the petitioner failed to lay a solid evidentiary foundation for injunctive relief under Article 199.
verdict.strengths: Counsel maintained respectful courtroom etiquette and correctly cited Article 4 of the Constitution to frame the grievance against arbitrary administrative action. The opening and closing remarks were concise and clearly articulated the core prayer for relief.
verdict.areas_for_improvement: Pay close attention to what the witness actually says; do not invent factual scenarios, such as claiming the witness stood across a busy road, after he testified he was never at the scene. Furthermore, you must substantiate documentary claims regarding lease agreements using the primary and secondary evidence provisions of the Qanun-e-Shahadat Order.
